ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 5 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Charlotte Brontë — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Prenatal visit at 13 weeks with the nuchal translucency scan and the low-dose aspirin decision

text.paragraph: Prenatal visit at 13 weeks with the nuchal translucency scan. [S]

Ms. Brontë returns at 13 weeks 1 day. She vomits two or three times a week and eats three meals and two snacks a day. She has taken ondansetron about twice a day this week and doxylamine-pyridoxine four tablets a day. Constipation has settled with diet. Her PUQE-24 score is 7. She has begun writing again in the mornings. The cell-free DNA result came back last week as low risk for trisomies 21, 18, and 13. She had the nuchal translucency scan this morning. She has had no headache, pain, or bleeding. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 1855-02-24; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Soft; uterus palpable above the pubic bone
Scan this morning: single live fetus, crown-rump length 70 mm, nuchal translucency 1.5 mm, nasal bone present, no structural abnormality seen
First pregnancy at 38 (elderly primigravida), single live intrauterine pregnancy dated by ultrasound at 7 weeks 1 day
S — Synthetic modern prenatal care anchored to the documented report that she was pregnant when she died; the pregnancy itself is questioned in one source (CLM-0019).
Nausea and vomiting of pregnancy, moderate (PUQE-24 score 10), with early weight loss, under evaluation for hyperemesis gravidarum

S — Synthetic presenting concern at the index visit, superseded by the hyperemesis gravidarum diagnosis at the sick visit; her documented "perpetual nausea" is D and the hyperemesis reading of it is R.

Hyperemesis gravidarum with metabolic disturbance: unable to keep fluids down, 7.4 percent weight loss, dehydration, hypokalemia, hyponatremia, hypochloremic alkalosis, low magnesium, and raised transaminases; PUQE-24 score 14
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis linked to her documented final illness and the retrospective hyperemesis interpretation; it is not asserted as her historical diagnosis.
Gestational transient thyrotoxicosis: suppressed TSH and mildly raised free T4 with hyperemesis, no goiter, eye signs, or tremor; no treatment needed
S — Synthetic finding that teaches the thyroid tests in hyperemesis; it echoes no documented illness.
